questions.question: A supervisor (star) design has eight agents: one hub and seven workers. How many links does the design have?
questions.explanation: A star on n agents has n − 1 links, one per worker, so 8 − 1 = 7. Lesson 50.1 gives the same count for the binary tree on eight agents. Twenty-eight is the count for the complete graph.

questions.question: Three agents each answer wrongly with probability 0.3. Their errors are independent, and all wrong answers are identical. What is the probability that the majority is wrong?
questions.explanation: The majority is wrong when at least two agents are wrong: 3(0.3)²(0.7) + (0.3)³ = 0.189 + 0.027 = 0.216. This is below the 0.300 error of one agent. The figure 0.163 is the five-agent value.

questions.question: Five peer agents run two all-to-all debate rounds. How many messages does the debate send?
questions.explanation: A debate sends R · n(n − 1) messages, here 2 · 5 · 4 = 40. The 20 is the count for one round, not two.

questions.question: A binary tree of eight agents has agent 0 at the root, agent 1 as its child, and agents 3 and 4 as children of agent 1. After agent 1 is removed, what share of ordered pairs of surviving agents can still reach each other?
questions.explanation: Removing agent 1 leaves three pieces: {0, 2, 5, 6} (4 agents), {3, 7} (2 agents) and {4} (1 agent). Reachable ordered pairs are 4 · 3 + 2 · 1 = 14, out of 7 · 6 = 42, which is 0.333. Lesson 50.1 gives 0.429 for removing the root, not agent 1.

questions.question: A contract net has six contractors, and every message is point-to-point. How many messages does one round use?
questions.explanation: Each contractor costs one announcement, one reply and at most one award, so one round costs 3N = 3 · 6 = 18. An all-to-all round among six agents would cost 30.

questions.question: A Byzantine agreement protocol must tolerate f = 2 faulty nodes in a group of n = 7. What is the smallest quorum size that makes any two quorums share at least f + 1 = 3 nodes?
questions.explanation: Two quorums of size q out of n share at least 2q − n nodes, which must be at least f + 1. For n = 7 and f = 2 this gives 2q − 7 ≥ 3, so q ≥ 5. A quorum of 4 shares only 1 node. Lesson 50.2 uses ⌈(n + f + 1)/2⌉ = ⌈10/2⌉ = 5.

questions.question: Nine voters each answer correctly with probability 0.7, and their errors are correlated with ρ = 0.3, meaning a shared draw happens 30% of the time. As the panel grows large, what is the ceiling on majority-vote accuracy?
questions.explanation: The accuracy is ρp + (1 − ρ) × maj(k, p), and maj tends to 1 as k grows. The ceiling is 0.3 · 0.7 + 0.7 = 0.91. Independent voters reach 0.99 at k = 31, but correlation caps the gain.

questions.question: In a sequential crew with default context, the writer receives the analyst's 90-word reply. The writer's system prompt and task together are 55 words. How many prompt words does the writer send?
questions.explanation: By default the writer receives only the previous task's output, so the prompt is 55 + 90 = 145 words. With context listing both earlier tasks, the prompt would be 55 + 120 + 90 = 265 words.

questions.question: A round-robin group chat stops after 25 messages of 60 words each. The prompt at turn t is 55 + 60t words, counting from t = 0. What is the total number of prompt words over the chat?
questions.explanation: The total is Σ(55 + 60t) for t = 0 to 24, which is 55 · 25 + 60 · 25 · 24 / 2 = 1375 + 18000 = 19375. The 1375 is only the fixed role and task part. The selector variant doubles the total to 38875.
